title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook 1) Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotations, game-day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. It is the single source of truth for operational response for production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated workers, private control plane).

1) Overview
2) Scope
3) Incident lifecycle (Detection -> Recovery -> Postmortem)
4) Alerting & triage
5) Runbook template & examples

overview: Purpose: provide clear, repeatable guidance so teams can detect, acknowledge, mitigate, and learn from incidents affecting Redwood's inference products. Goals: minimize customer impact, meet SLOs where possible, communicate clearly, and rapidly restore service. Audience: engineers, SREs, support, product, and GTM teams.
scope: Applies to all production services and external customer-facing endpoints including: Redwood API (hosted inference), Redwood Dedicated control plane, Private deployment control plane, and critical infra services (routing, KV cache, auth). Development/test environments follow separate non-production guidance.
incident_response_phases:
1) Detect & Alert: automated monitoring and user reports trigger an incident.
2) Triage: on-call reviews alerts, assigns severity, and determines impact.
3) Mitigate: runbooks executed to reduce customer impact (fallbacks, throttles, rollback).
4) Recover: restore normal operation and verify SLOs.
5) Postmortem & Action: document root cause, corrective actions, and owners.
6) Review: follow up on action completion and measure effectiveness.
detection_and_alerting:
Monitoring sources: Prometheus alerts, synthetic checks (latency QPS), tracing error rates (Jaeger), customer error reports (Zendesk), and automated quality monitors (regression alerts from Redwood Optimize).
Primary alert tiers: P0 (SEV1) - total outage or >50% latency/error SLO breach; P1 (SEV2) - degraded performance affecting core customers; P2 (SEV3) - local service degradation, limited impact.
Alert channels: PagerDuty (primary), #incidents Slack channel (secondary), SMS to escalation on-call for P0. Alerts must include runbook link, alert firing query, and recent trend data.
triage_playbook:
Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty.
2) Create incident in incident tracker (Confluence incident page template + internal incident ID).
3) Determine severity using Severity Matrix (see Postmortem section).
4) Identify affected services & customers (use routing dashboard and support ticket queue).
5) Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, Engineering Lead, SRE Lead.
6) If P0/P1, notify execs via #exec-ops and send initial status page entry.
7) Start mitigation steps from the relevant runbook.
Triage inputs: service logs, recent deploys, autoscaler metrics, GPU utilization, fallback invocation counts, KV cache hit/miss rates.
runbook_template:
Each runbook should include:
- Title and service (e.g., Redwood API — model-router)
- Purpose / impact description
- Owner and escalation contact list
- Preconditions (what to check first)
- Step-by-step mitigation steps (numbered)
- Verification steps to confirm recovery
- Safe rollback / fallback recipes
- Post-incident notes and links to dashboards/logs
Example fields:
Title: model-router-high-latency
Owner: runtime-team@redwood.com
Preconditions: Latency > 1500ms p95 for >5 min AND error rate increase >2x
Steps: 1) Check recent deploys (ci-cd job IDs). 2) Roll back to previous tag if deploy within 30 min. 3) Increase routing pool for dedicated customers. 4) Engage autoscaling / add GPU nodes.
Verification: p95 latency falls below 600ms and error rate returns to baseline for 10 minutes.
example_runbooks: Redwood API — Model Router High Latency: Steps to diagnose routing hotspots, verify KV cache health, and perform safe rollback to previous revision.
Dedicated GPUs — Node OOMs: How to drain, cordon, and reprovision nodes, and how to enable degraded-mode routing for reserved workloads.
Private Control Plane — Auth Outage: Steps to switch to emergency auth key, validate tokens, and notify affected customers via status page.
KV Cache Evictions — Elevated Miss Rate: Steps to identify hot prefixes, disable cache warming jobs temporarily, and throttle low-priority requests.
postmortem_process:
Severity definitions: P0 (SEV1) — customer-visible outage or SLO loss >4 hours; P1 (SEV2) — partial outage or SLO loss 15 minutes-4 hours; P2 (SEV3) — minor degradations.
Postmortem timeline:
1) Within 72 hours: IC creates preliminary incident page with timeline and known facts.
2) Within 7 calendar days: write a full postmortem draft including timeline, root cause analysis (RCA), and at least 1-3 action items with owners and due dates.
3) Review: schedule cross-functional review (engineering, SRE, product, support) and update postmortem.
4) Close: when all action items are tracked and a verification plan defined.
Postmortem format (must be present on Confluence incident page): Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root Cause, Contributing Factors, Actions Taken, Corrective Actions, Owner(s), Verification Plan, Lessons Learned.
Blamelessness: focus on systemic fixes, not individuals. Include links to related commits, runbook executions, and monitoring graphs.
oncall_rotations:
Rotation models: Primary/secondary weekly rotation for SRE on-call; 24/7 PagerDuty primary for P0 and P1 incidents. Engineering teams maintain on-call for their services with a recommended cadence of 1 week.
Responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: acknowledge alerts, perform first-triage, run immediate mitigations, escalate as needed.
- Secondary on-call: provide backup and handle pager escalations, own after-hours code changes when primary is unavailable.
- On-call handover: each shift must update the rotation board with outstanding incidents, ongoing mitigations, and expected maintenance windows.
Shift guidelines: no more than 1 week of high-intensity on-call per month per engineer; ensure two consecutive days off after a P0 response where possible.
escalation_matrix:
Escalation rules:
1) If unresolved after 15 minutes (P0) escalate to team lead.
2) If unresolved after 30 minutes escalate to SRE lead and oncall-sre-manager.
3) If unresolved after 60 minutes escalate to Director of Engineering and Customer-facing comms activated.
4) For customer-impacting P0s that cross billing / SLA thresholds, notify Legal and Finance.
Escalation contacts (roles only in doc): Primary on-call -> Team Lead -> SRE Lead -> Engineering Director -> VP Eng / Exec. PagerDuty escalation policies must mirror this matrix.
game_days:
Purpose: exercise incident response, validate runbooks, and improve cross-team coordination.
Frequency: at least quarterly for platform-critical scenarios and annually full-stack.
Typical scenarios: regional outage, model regression causing hallucinations, mass KV cache eviction, autoscaler failure.
Game day format:
1) Pre-brief: objectives and scope (no surprise production changes).
2) Inject: trigger simulated alert (synthetic traffic or theater).
3) Execute: on-call follows real runbooks and logs actions.
4) Debrief: immediate 30-60 minute review, then 7-day follow-up capturing action items.
Success criteria: runbooks executed without major blockers, restoration within target RTOs, clear comms to stakeholders.
status_page_templates: Initial STATUS (short): We are investigating elevated latency impacting text generation for hosted API customers. Engineers have been engaged and mitigation steps are in progress. Next update in 30 minutes.

Update STATUS (mid): Root cause identified (model-router throttling after recent deploy). We have rolled back the deploy and latency is improving; partial service restored to most customers. Next update in 60 minutes.
Resolved STATUS: Issue resolved. All services are operating normally. We will publish a postmortem within 7 days with root cause and corrective actions.
customer_communications_templates:
Initial customer-facing email/SaaS notice: Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference service - [Short summary]
Body: We are currently investigating an incident affecting [service]. Some customers may experience increased latency or errors. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation and we will provide updates on the status page and via support. Estimated next update: 30 minutes.

Follow-up/update: Subject: Update on incident affecting [service]
Body: We have identified the likely cause (brief RCA) and are executing a rollback / mitigation. Impact reduced for most customers; some may still experience degraded performance. We will follow up when the service is fully restored. For urgent concerns contact support@redwood.com.

Resolution & postmortem notice: Subject: Incident resolved - [service] (Postmortem to follow)
Body: The issue has been resolved as of [time]. Impact: [summary of affected customers, duration]. Root cause: [brief root cause]. Actions taken: [list]. Next steps: action items and timeframe for completion. Contact: support@redwood.com for follow-ups.
ownership_and_contacts:
Standard roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns incident lifecycle and communications until handoff.
- Communications Lead: drafts and posts status page and customer comms.
- Engineering Lead: drives technical mitigation and recovery.
- SRE Lead: coordinates infra actions (scaling, node reprovision).
- Postmortem Owner: author and track remediation items.
On-call roster is maintained in the oncall rotation board (internal link). Primary contact groups: runtime-team@redwood.com, infra-sre@redwood.com, support@redwood.com.
sla_and_slos:
Typical SLOs to reference during incidents:
- API availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted inference endpoints.
- p95 latency: < 600ms for text generation under normal load.
- Embedding throughput SLA: 99.9% for bulk jobs during business hours.
When SLOs are at risk, prioritize mitigations that reduce customer impact even if short-term cost increases (e.g., temporary overprovisioning, bypassing caches for critical traffic).
metrics_and_dashboarding:
Dashboards to check on first triage:
- Global: requests/sec, errors/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, request queue length.
- Runtime: GPU utilization, model load time, KV cache hit/miss, batch size distribution.
- Orchestration: autoscaler actions, queue backlog, node health.
All dashboards are linked from the incident template and should include a 'last 60m' and 'last 24h' view for context. Ensure synthetic checks span every region and major model families.
runbook_change_process:
Runbooks are living documents. To update a runbook:
1) Create PR in docs repo with change summary.
2) Add a reviewer from the owner team.
3) After approval, update the Confluence runbook page and add a 'last_tested' date.
4) Mandatory: runbooks for critical flows must be exercised in a game day at least annually.
Record version and last tested date in the runbook header.
sop_checklist: Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create incident page
Assign Incident Commander and Communications Lead
Post initial status on status.redwood.com and #incidents Slack
Execute relevant runbook mitigations and record commands/outputs
Confirm recovery with verification steps in runbook
Track action items with owners and due dates
Schedule game day if runbook or process gaps discovered
